text:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing a capacity gap in us-west1 causing ~120 GPU pods in Pending. Most requests are getting routed to us-west1-a and it's saturated, other AZs have free slots but scheduler seems to prefer the anchored pool.

sam: Any errors in events? kube-scheduler logs?

maya: Events snippet from one of the pending pods:
```
Normal   FailedScheduling  2m   default-scheduler  0/16 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 2 node(s) didn't match PodAffinity/AntiAffinity.
```

henry: Hmm looks like a mix of taints + anti-affinity. Did we recently roll the rack taint policy in us-west1-b?

lia: Yes, we shipped the `rack-isolation` taint to reduce noisy-neighbor risk last deploy. It landed only on b/c to keep a warm pool in a/b. Could be over-constraining tiny-gang workloads.

maya: Also noticed scheduler events showing preferredAffinity scoring strongly toward a. Full log line: `PreferAvoidPodsScore: node us-west1-a-xyz score 950/1000` so there's a hard bias.

sam: Quick repro: run `kubectl get pods -o wide -n ml | grep Pending | head -n 10` — can you paste output?

maya: Pasted below:
```
ml-model-aaa   Pending   0/1 nodes available   8m   nvidia.com/gpu=1   us-west1-a
ml-model-bbb   Pending   0/1 nodes available   12m  nvidia.com/gpu=1   us-west1-a
...
```

henry: Two vectors to fix fast: 1) temporarily relax the rack-isolation taint on us-west1-b (add toleration for our ML pod SA) so pods can land; 2) broaden anti-affinity rules for tiny-gang class to allow cross-az placement for latency-tolerant jobs. Which do we want as hotfix?

lia: I'd prefer 1) as immediate mitigation — patching taint toleration is smallest blast radius. We should also roll an experiment to tweak scheduler scoring weights for affinity next week.

maya: I'll run the toleration rollout on canary namespace and watch. Command I'll use: `kubectl patch poddefaults ml-default -p '{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"rack-isolation","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule","tolerationSeconds":3600}]}}'` — will post results.

infra-bot: deploy started by maya: patch poddefaults/ml-default; watch logs at https://ci.redwood/infralog/patch-1758765432

sam: FYI we should also check warm-pool autoscaler triggers — it hasn't scaled up for a while because of a threshold bug (tracked in ENG-INFRA-214). If the warm pool had 4 more slots, this would be less painful.

maya: Canary applied to `ml-canary` namespace. First two pods scheduled to us-west1-b successfully. Observability: tokenized allocation shows GPU-util on b jumped from 12%->46%.

henry: Nice. Can we automate a short-term scheduler fallback to distribute when AZ skew > 60%? Might be a useful safety valve.

lia: Opened a short RFC thread: /link to rfc-drafts (will ping here). For now, let's do the toleration rollback after 1h if we see no regressions. maya, monitor for preemptions and latency.

maya: Will monitor. If anything odd, I'll escalate to oncall. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: Follow-up tasks: - ENG-INFRA-214 (warm pool scale) - ENG-SCHED-88 (affinity weight tweak) - ENG-PLAT-ops: add a dashboard alert for AZ allocation imbalance (>60% occupancy one AZ).

lia: Adding alert and owner.

maya: Last note: cost impact — if we keep falling back to on-demand in other AZs, monthly GPU spend could jump ~8-12% for this tenant cohort. We'll track chargeback.

infra-bot: incident tracker updated: ticket INF-1758765432 created for zone-capacity-gap; assignees: maya, sam, henry.

maya: Ok closing thread; will post a short postmortem if we need one after the 24h window.
